narr: Anomalously high moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Barry encouraged the development of tropical downpours across West Texas and Southeast New Mexico. These downpours resulted in Flash Flooding for portions of the area.
ev: Emergency Management reported many evacuations of campgrounds in the Big Bend area due to flash flooding. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar. No damages were reported.
Extremely heavy rain around Marfa and Fort Davis produced widespread street flooding. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar. No damage was reported.

Emergency Management in Alpine reported one home inundated by flooding due to heavy rainfall and numerous road closures by local authorities. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar. The total cost of damages is also estimated.
A Texas Parks and Wildlife Park Ranger reported high water over FM 170 East at Terneros Creek. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar. No damage was reported.
Emergency Management reported high water due to flash flooding impacting Highway 87 in southeastern Dawson County. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar. No damage was reported.
Park rangers at the Big Bend reported flood water rushing through Long Draw Creek over FM 170. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar. No damage was reported.
Multiple road closures were reported across Dawson County due to flooded roadways. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar. No damage was reported.
The Drive Texas website indicated water was covering the roadway of the Business I-20 north service road near East Loop 338. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar. No damage was reported.

Emergency management reported 21 vehicles stalled in high water due to flash flooding across various portions of Midland, TX. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar. The total cost of damages is also estimated.
